hypothesis: The two failed holding samples (.30s=0.020494, .31s=0.024643 m/s) persist because the holding-window tip-speed penalty, though demonstrably active and correctly computed, is too weak relative to the dominant terminal-position cost and to early seed-based termination; raising only holding_tip_speed_weight 0.05 to 0.10 should lower predicted holding-node tip speed and thereby reduce the sampled .30-.35s holding overspeed under recovery-enabled execution.
limitations: No unique causal attribution; structure and control remain jointly reported and prior warm initializations may carry earlier changed actions.
Local raw objective values under different weights have different cost definitions and must not be used to rank arms.
Sampled 6-point inclusive holding window is not a continuous-time guarantee.
Predicted holding speed comes from the projected GVS prediction, not the full serial backend.
One development closed loop and at most one confirmation only; no real-time, hardware or model-superiority claim.
revision_or_stop_rule: If this single-weight development loop reduces the sampled holding max speed and, ideally, brings the .31s sample below 0.02 m/s without breaching position limits, run one exact control_confirmation with identical configuration, seed and initial state, then stop after it. If it does not improve, do not spend the second launch on confirmation; STOP and report the .025-.10 single-weight range as insufficient under the frozen configuration.
weakening_observation: Weakening if the sampled holding max speed stays at/near the baseline 0.024643 m/s (or rises) while the predicted first-node speeds fall, showing predicted-speed reduction does not translate through the model/backend mismatch; or if the raw objectives are compared to rank arms (different weight definitions make raw sums non-comparable). A null/varied result would point to early termination and prediction-vs-actual mismatch, not the soft weight, as dominant.
